title: Portugal vs. Georgia vs. Costa Rica: The 2026 Digital Nomad Visa and Tax Breakdown for Non-US Residents Running a US LLC

# Portugal vs. Georgia vs. Costa Rica: The 2026 Digital Nomad Visa and Tax Breakdown for Non-US Residents Running a US LLC

If you run a U.S. LLC as a non-U.S. resident, where you live determines how much tax you pay. Three countries stand out in 2026 for combining accessible digital nomad visas with genuinely favorable tax treatment: Portugal, Georgia, and Costa Rica. Here is exactly how each one stacks up.

---

## Why Your LLC's Tax Exposure Depends on Where You Live

A single-member U.S. LLC owned by a non-U.S. resident is tax-transparent by default. The IRS does not tax it at the entity level if the income is foreign-sourced. But your country of residence has its own opinion on that income, and that is where the real tax story begins.

> **Note:** "Foreign-sourced" typically means your U.S. LLC's clients and business activities are outside the U.S. If you have U.S.-sourced income, different rules apply. Always confirm with a cross-border tax professional before choosing a base.

---

## Portugal: The NHR 2.0 Reality in 2026

Portugal replaced the original Non-Habitual Resident (NHR) regime with IFICI (Incentivo Fiscal à Captação de Investimento e Conhecistas) at the start of 2024. By 2026, it is now the established framework for newcomers.

### Visa Path

Portugal's Digital Nomad Visa (D8) remains active and well-structured in 2026. Requirements include:

- Minimum monthly income of €3,680 (four times the 2026 national minimum wage of €920)
- Proof of remote work or self-employment for a non-Portuguese employer or clients
- Private health insurance
- Processing time: 2 to 4 months via consulate

> **Note:** The D8 income threshold increased from €3,480 in 2025 to €3,680 in 2026, following Portugal's minimum wage rise from €870 to €920. If you are using older guides, that figure is now outdated.

### Tax Treatment Under IFICI

Qualifying professionals receive a flat 20% tax rate on Portuguese-sourced income. Foreign income, including distributions from your U.S. LLC, may be exempt under the territorial exemption clause, depending on your activity type.

**Key costs and considerations:**

| Factor | Detail |
|---|---|
| Flat income tax rate | 20% on qualifying Portuguese-sourced income |
| Foreign income exemption | Possible under IFICI, activity-dependent |
| Social security contributions | Mandatory for self-employed; roughly 21.4% |
| Cost of living (Lisbon) | €2,500 to €3,500/month for a comfortable lifestyle |
| NHR 2.0 duration | 10 years |

Portugal is excellent for EU access, infrastructure, and lifestyle. The tax math is favorable if your LLC income qualifies as foreign-sourced and exempt. Social security obligations are the main cost to plan around.

---

## Georgia: The Simplest Tax Structure of the Three

Georgia (the country, not the U.S. state) operates a strict territorial tax system. If your income is earned outside Georgia, the Georgian tax authority does not touch it. Period.

### Visa Path

Georgia offers visa-free entry of up to 365 days for citizens of most countries, including most of Europe, Latin America, and several Asian nations. For longer stays, the Remotely from Georgia program and residence permits are available.

### Tax Treatment

If your U.S. LLC income is generated from clients and operations entirely outside Georgia, your Georgian tax liability is effectively zero on that income. The territorial system is straightforward and well-established.

**Key costs and considerations:**

| Factor | Detail |
|---|---|
| Tax on foreign-sourced LLC income | 0% under territorial rules |
| Personal income tax (if applicable) | 20% flat on Georgian-sourced income |
| Cost of living (Tbilisi) | €800 to €1,500/month |
| Ease of banking | Good; TBC Bank and Bank of Georgia serve non-residents well |
| Visa-free stay | Up to 365 days for eligible nationalities |

Georgia is the lowest-cost, lowest-tax option of the three. The tradeoff is that it lacks EU access and the infrastructure familiarity some nomads prefer.

---

## Costa Rica: The Rentista and Digital Nomad Option in Latin America

Costa Rica launched its Digital Nomad Visa in 2022 and has refined it steadily. In 2026, it remains one of the most practical Latin America bases for LLC owners wanting time zone alignment with U.S. clients.

### Visa Path

- Minimum monthly income of $3,000 (or $4,000 for applicants with dependents)
- Income must come from outside Costa Rica
- Visa valid for 1 year, renewable for 1 additional year
- Processing time: 1 to 3 months

### Tax Treatment

Costa Rica operates a territorial tax system. Foreign-sourced income, including LLC distributions from U.S. operations serving non-Costa Rican clients, is not subject to Costa Rican income tax.

**Key costs and considerations:**

| Factor | Detail |
|---|---|
| Tax on foreign-sourced LLC income | 0% under territorial rules |
| Cost of living (San José) | €1,500 to €2,500/month |
| U.S. time zone alignment | Yes; Central Time (CST/CDT) |
| Visa duration | 1 year, renewable once |
| Path to residency | Rentista or Pensionado residency available after |

Costa Rica suits nomads who need overlap with U.S. clients and prefer Latin America without sacrificing modern amenities.

---

## Side-by-Side Comparison

| Criteria | Portugal | Georgia | Costa Rica |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tax on foreign LLC income | Possibly exempt | 0% | 0% |
| Cost of living | High | Low | Medium |
| Visa difficulty | Moderate | Very easy | Moderate |
| EU access | Yes | No | No |
| U.S. time zone alignment | No | No | Yes |

---

> **Note:** None of this replaces professional tax advice. Each situation depends on your nationality, LLC structure, client locations, and personal circumstances.
